factual_fidelity.justification: The original page preserves all supplied specifications, including the distinct diameters, price, compatibility list, oven limit, and lid exclusion. The targeted revisions retain the core care instructions, but replacing the care section removes its explicit hot-handle and oven-mitt reminder, leaving only the earlier warning that permits dry towels. The pre-seasoning revision also introduces an unsupported promise of reduced oil use.
quotes: need less oil from the very first meal
Use oven mitts or dry towels every time you handle the skillet.
factual_fidelity.improvement: Keep an explicit 'Handles get hot; use oven mitts' reminder in the revised care section, especially beside stovetop drying, and remove the unsubstantiated reduced-oil claim.

useful_persuasion.justification: The page connects handles, spouts, and oven compatibility to practical cooking tasks and includes a clear purchase action. However, some benefits exceed the supplied evidence: reduced oil from the first meal, splatter containment and easier lifting from rim width, and universal stovetop phrasing. These weaken otherwise useful beginner-focused persuasion.
quotes: Start on the burner, finish in the oven without switching pans.
A long main handle plus a helper handle gives you a steady two-hand grip when moving a full pan.
the wider top edge helps contain splatter and makes lifting easier
useful_persuasion.improvement: Limit compatibility language to the four listed stovetop types, remove unsupported rim benefits, and describe pre-seasoning as a starting seasoning layer rather than guaranteeing first-meal oil savings.

readability_and_voice.justification: The page is welcoming, well organized, and easy to scan, with separate benefits, specifications, care, and purchase sections. The final care revision gives beginners concrete tools, sequence, and a useful visual cue for oil quantity. Editorial requests are addressed directly, although the revised care section should retain the handling warning and explain cooling before washing.
quotes: Cast iron doesn’t have to be intimidating.
Caring for this skillet comes down to three habits: wash it by hand, dry it right away, and rub on a thin layer of oil.
Wipe away any excess so the skillet looks dark but not oily. Let it cool, then store.
readability_and_voice.improvement: Add a brief safe-handling cue before washing and an oven-mitt reminder during heat drying, while preserving the concise three-step format.

overall_impression: A clear, practical beginner product page with strong organization and actionable care guidance. Unsupported performance embellishments and a weakened hot-handle warning across revisions prevent a higher score.
